bull.b: The combination of substantial liquidity, meaningful working capital and no debt gives Streamex flexibility to fund product development and institutional onboarding. Management estimates immediately available funds cover about 18 months and total liquidity about three years if revenue does not grow.

The sharp reduction in operating expenses and quarterly losses shows that management has begun improving the cost structure. Sustaining these reductions would extend liquidity, lower the revenue threshold needed for scale, and provide a stronger base for future investment in the platform.

Completed custody, attestation, brokerage and liquidity arrangements address important infrastructure requirements for institutional participation. This broadens distribution capability and may support durable adoption of tokenized gold if the company converts its partnerships and integrations into recurring holders.

bear.b: Streamex has not yet demonstrated the revenue scale needed to absorb its cost base. Extremely large losses relative to minimal and volatile revenue indicate weak earnings quality and make durable profitability dependent on substantial growth in AUM, transaction activity and other platform income.

Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits mean the business is consuming capital rather than funding itself. Even with reported liquidity, continued burn increases dependence on outside funding or successful commercialization and can constrain the pace of investment if adoption develops slowly.

The platform remains early-stage, with limited external ownership and modest AUM, so commercial traction is not yet broad-based. Unremediated material control weaknesses add execution and reporting risk while management seeks institutional allocations, integrations and wider product adoption.
